content.title: About
content.content: Goat milk is the milk of the domestic goat. It is white, slightly sweet, and has a characteristic mild tang. It is drunk, added to porridge and baked goods, and used to make yogurt, cottage cheese, and cheeses such as chèvre and feta. Goat milk is close to cow milk in composition but differs in the structure of its fat and proteins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The fat globules in goat milk are smaller, so it separates less and mixes more easily.
Goat milk is whiter than cow milk because goats convert beta-carotene into vitamin A.
Goat milk is made into chèvre, feta, and other cheeses.
Goats were among the first domesticated animals.
A goat gives less milk than a cow.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium is needed for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and B2
items.content: These vitamins support vision, skin, and metabolism.

items.title: May be easier to digest
items.content: Some people find goat milk easier on the stomach, but scientific evidence for this is limited.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Goat milk contains lactose, so it is not suitable for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: With an allergy to cow milk proteins, goat milk is usually unsafe too because of cross-reaction.

items.title: Raw milk
items.content: Raw milk may contain Brucella, Campylobacter, and Listeria; it should be boiled or drunk pasteurized.

items.title: For infants
items.content: Ordinary goat milk is not suitable for infants in place of formula; there are special goat milk-based formulas for them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink goat milk pasteurized or boiled, add it to porridge, cocoa, baked goods, shakes, and smoothies, and make yogurt, cottage cheese, and cheeses from it. Raw milk must be boiled.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store milk in the refrigerator in a closed container and use it by the date on the package; after opening, within a few days. Milk can be frozen. Discard milk that smells sour.
